_comment: Address -> entity map. This is the ground truth for identification method (a),
the known-label lookup, and it is why the tool can name an exchange at all.
WHY these addresses are knowable: an exchange cannot hide its hot wallets.
It must publish deposit addresses to millions of users and settle enormous
volume through a small number of wallets, so its on-chain fingerprint is
large, stable and public. That is the asymmetry the whole tool rests on -
the criminal's fresh wallets are anonymous, but the exit point is not.
STARTER SET ONLY (~28 entries). Seeded by hand from Etherscan's public label
cloud and widely-published incident reporting. Expand later from:
- GraphSense TagPacks (https://github.com/graphsense/graphsense-tagpacks)
- Etherscan public label cloud (https://etherscan.io/labelcloud)
- OFAC SDN crypto address list (sanctions flags)
Indian VASPs (WazirX, CoinDCX, ZebPay) are deliberately ABSENT rather than
guessed - they matter most for the SAHYOG workflow, so they should be added
from a verified TagPack rather than from memory.
Keys must be lowercase. 'type' is one of: exchange | mixer | bridge.
Every underscore-prefixed key is ignored by the loader.
VERIFIED: every address below was checked on-chain (nonce / contract code /
balance) and shows activity consistent with its label. Re-run that check
after adding entries - a wrong address here silently produces a confident
and completely false attribution, which is the worst failure this tool has.
